claim.qualifier: Tesla advertises 250 kW peak Supercharging for Model Y on V3+ Superchargers

sources.name: Car and Driver — 2026 Model Y Long Range AWD Test (mfr spec table reproduced)

reality.qualifier: 250 kW sustained roughly 5–22% SOC, ~6 minutes, with battery preconditioned. EVKX systematic curve: rate drops to ~189 kW by 20% SOC, ~135 kW by 30%, ~80 kW by 50%.
reality.verbatim_quote: the current Tesla Model Y, Model 3 vehicles with the 2170 battery cells can only charge at the current maximum V3 Supercharger charging rate (~250kW) for just ~6 minutes before the charging rate starts to taper down.

sources.name: EVKX — Tesla Model Y Long Range systematic charging curve
Tesla Motors Club forum — owner-reported charging-curve data, multiple posters in thread

narrative_one_liner: Tesla's 250 kW peak Supercharging is sustained ~6 minutes (5–22% SOC); rate halves by 30% SOC.
narrative: Tesla's 250 kW peak Supercharging is sustained for roughly 6 minutes between 5–22% state of charge, then tapers. By 30% SOC the rate has dropped to ~135 kW; by 50% it's ~80 kW. The headline number is real but is achieved only briefly under specific preconditioning conditions; it does not represent the average rate during a typical 10–80% road-trip charge.
methodology_notes: EVKX publishes per-percent SOC charging-rate tables aggregated across multiple sessions; reproducible. TMC forum thread provides owner-reported corroboration with N>10 distinct posters in the cited thread.
caveats: EVKX is a relatively low-profile but methodologically transparent source; would benefit from corroboration by Out of Spec Reviews instrumented data.
TMC forum data quality varies; the cited thread's quality was assessed for engagement and consistency but not formally graded.
alternative_explanations: Battery temperature outside ideal range could produce the observed taper; sources note preconditioning was applied.
Charger-side power sharing (multi-stall cabinets) can produce the observed plateau but is documented as a separate phenomenon.
